Satellite Money Orders 
*241. SHRI C. P. THIRUNAVUKKARASU: WUl the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Department of Posts has achieved the expected traffic of 
Satellite Money Orders; 
(b) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) what steps Government are taking to improve the traffic of Satellite 
Money Order transfer? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS (SHRr PRAMOD 
MAHAJAN): (a) to (c) Sir, a statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA        [6 December, 2001] 
Statement 
The Government had approved setting up of 75 Very Small Aperture 
Terminal (VSAT) stations as a part of 8th Five Year plan for transmission of 
Money Orders through Satellite system for cutting down delay in transmission 
and reducing manual handling of Money Orders thereby the cost of operation. 
The process of installation of VSAT network started towards the middle of 
1995 and 77 VSAT stations in place of  75 were installed by the middle of 
financial year 1996-97. 
The technology adopted for the VSAT was Code Division Multiple Access 
(CDMA) based micro-earth station having a bandwidth of 1.2 KBPS installed 
at Sikandarabad in Bulandshahar, Uttar Pradesh. Seventy-seven VSAT 
installed were networked with 610 Extended Satellite Money Order (ESMO) 
stations. 
At the time of planning for the VSAT system during 1992-93, the system 
was expected to capture about 25% of the total traffic of about 9.8 crores 
Money Orders. While six circles have captured more than 25% of the traffic, 
others could not do that on account of limitation of the technology like low 
bandwidth of 1.2 KBPS and capacity problem of the Remote Area Business 
Management Network (RABMN). With the increase in the bandwidth and by 
increasing the network by adding more ESMOs to the system, the flow of 
traffic could be increased to about 11.5 per cent of the overall traffic of 12 
crores Money Orders handled by the Department during 2000-01. 
Simultaneously, the Department on the advice of an Expert group took 
steps to set up high speed VSAT system on Time Division Multiple Access 
(TDMA) with 64 KBPS bandwidth. It has already installed 135 such high 
speed VSATs and 15 are under user testing. These stations are networked 
through 1350 ESMO stations. To this 400 more ESMO stations will be added 
to increase the flow of traffic through satellite. The old 77 VSATs on Code 
Division Multiple

Access (CDMA) technology are also netw orked to the high-speed system to 
enable the Money Order traffic to be transmitted through the system.

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
New System of recruitment for All India Services 
*242. SHRI   P.   PRABHAKAR   REDDY:   Will   the   PRIME 
MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the method of recruitment to the All India 
Services is set to undergo a major revision; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
4 

[6 December, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) whether the new system would take into account the special requirements 
for the millennium leading to an era of a new generation of reforms; and 
(d) by when the new selection process is likely to be put in place? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, 
PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA 
RAJE): (a) to (d) No, Sir. There is no proposal to revise the method of 
recruitment to the All India Services. However, the Union Public Service 
Commission has appointed a Committee under the Chairmanship of Prof. Y. K. 
Alagh to review the present scheme of Examination for the Combined Civil 
Services Examination. This does not in clude the Indian Forest Service. The 
present review has been undertaken keeping in view the changes in administrative 
environment, liberalization, globalization, technological advancements and changing 
role of the State and the bureaucracy . The Government is yet to receive 
recommendations of Union Public Service Commission.

Handing over of NH-52 to BRO 
*249. DR. ARUN KUMAR SARMA: Will the Minister of ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it has been decided to hand over National Highway-52 to the 
Border Roads Organisation; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor, the date of decision and actual execution; 
(c) the details of the outstanding liabilities to the contractors and the 
category-wise strength and probable fate of the employees in the light of the 
said decision, working under Assam PWD for National Highway-52; 
(d) the details of the improvement and repair plan, including target set for 
conversion into four lane; and 
9 

 
RAJYA SABHA [6 December, 2001] 
(e) the date of allocation and implementation status of bridge at Jaladia 
Suti by BRO? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (MAJ. GEN. (RETD.) B.C. 
KHANDURI): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. NH-52 in Assam has been entrusted to 
Border Roads Organisation (BRO) vide Government of India Notification 
dated 16.8.2001. The State PWD, however, has not yet handed over the 
National Highway to BRO. The decision to entrust the road to BRO was 
taken as the State Government was not able to utilize the allocation of funds 
for maintenance and development of National Highway effectively. 
(c) There are 22 ongoing improvement works on NH-52. The total 
sanctioned cost of these works is Rs. 38.12 crore and an expenditure 
of Rs. 11.70 crore has been incurred upto September, 2001. Some of 
the works are going on for last 6 to 7 years. The present outstanding 
liabilities of Plan works to the contractors is Rs. 3.45 crore. 
NH works are executed by the State PW D on agency basis. The record of 
State PWD employees is not maintained by the Ministry. Fate of the 
employees is to be decided by Government of Assam. 
(d) Four laning of NH-52 is not envisaged at present. However, 
the BRO has been advised to prepare plan for improvement of the 
NH. 
The development and maintenance of National Highway is a continuing 
process and it is difficult to indicate the date for completion of development. 
(e) Construction of Jalakia Suti bridge was sanctioned in 
November, 1998. The progress upto October, 2001 is 56.48%. The 
work is likely to be completed by March, 2002. 
Rise in unemployment 
*250. SHRI K. B. KRISHNA MURTHY : Will the Minister of LABOUR 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Planning Commission has admitted rise in unemployment 
after the economic reforms were launched; 
10 

[6 December, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) whether the employment growth rate slipped during 1993-94 to 1999-
2000 in comparison to earlier decade (1983-84 to 1993-94) and if so, to what 
extent; 
(c) whether the incidence of unemployment among youths (15-29 age 
group) is also rising and if so, to what extent; and 
(d) what steps-programmes Government  are likely to take-launch to 
create more employment opportunities? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) Estimates 
of employment and unemployment are obtained through National Sample 
Surveys carried out by National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) from 
time to time. According to these survey results, the incidence of 
unemployment [as per Usual Principal and subsidiary Status Approach 
(UPSS)] has increased from 1.90% in 1993-94 to 2.23% in 1999-2000. 
(b) The rate of growth of employment during 1993-94 to 1999-2000 was 
estimated to be 0.98% per annum compared to 2.04% per annum auring 1983 
to 1993-94. 
(c) The incidence of unemployment among youth (age group 15-29) has 
increased from 4.6% in 1993-94 to 5.4% in 1999-2000. 
(d) The Approach to the Tenth Five Year Plan has recognized the 
importance of providing -gainful high quality employment to the additions to 
the labour force and it is listed as one of the monitorable objectives for the 
Tenth Plan and beyond. The growth strategy of Tenth Plan would lay 
emphasis on rapid growth of those sectors which are most likely to create high 
quality employment opportunities and deal with the policy constraints which 
discourage growth of employment. Par ticular attention will be paid to the 
policy environment influencing a wide range of economic activities which 
have a large employment potential. These include sectors such as 
construction, real estate and housing, transport, Small Scale Industry (SSI), 
modern retailing, Information Technology (IT) enabled services and a range 
of other new services which need to be promoted through supportive policies. 
Emphasis will also be laid on tourism to ensure realization of full potential of 
this activity. 
11 

RAJYA SABHA [6 December, 2001] 
Employment Strategy in the Tenth Plan will focus on employment growth 
and on the qualitative aspects of employment. In order to enable the poor to  
access the opportunities and to ensure consistency between the requirement 
and availability of skills, emphasis will also be placed on skill development.

identification and rehabilitation of potentially viable sick industries, which 
inter alia, includes institutional mechanism in the form of State Level Inter 
Institutional Committees, special rehabilitation cells in banks and State 
financial institutions and elaborate guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of 
India for extending rehabilitation assistance to eligible units. Further, with a 
view to strengthen the SSI sector and enhance its competitiveness

Incentives for Software Sector 
1. Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme (EPCG) has been rationalised 
and extended uniformly to all sectors without any threshold limit on 
payment of 5% duty. 
2. Approvals for all foreign direct investment proposals relating to the 
Information Technology sector, with the exception of Business-to-
consumer (B2C) e-commerce are under the automatic route. 
3. Software Technology Parks (STP) Scheme is implemented under the 
aegis of the Ministry of Information Technology through a single 
window mechanism of the Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee 
(IMSC). 
4. Accelerated depreciation norms for co mputers and computer peripherals 
for units under Export Oriented schemes (EOU/ EPZ/STP/EHTP) have 
been enhanced. These shall stand de preciated to overall limit of 90% 
over a period of 3 years instead of around 5 years earlier. 
5. DTA access upto 50% of the FOB va lue of export is permitted for 
software units under EOU/STP schemes. 
6. In . the 2000-01 Budget, Customs duty on Computers and Peripherals 
had been reduced from 20% to 15% and continues to be same. The 
Customs duty on all storage devices, integrated circuits, 
microprocessors, data display tubes and deflection components of colour 
monitors also continues at 0%. In the 2001-02 Budget, Customs duty on 
Information Technology Agreement (ITA-1) items of WTO (IT and 
Telecom products) has been reduced from existing 20—25% to 15%. 
7. Information Technology Software is exempted from Customs and Excise 
Duty. 
8. EOU/EPZ/STP/EHTP units are exempt ed from payment of Income Tax 
on export profits, upto 2010, in terms of Section 10A and   10B  of the  
Income  Tax  Act.   On  site  development  of

11. Exemption of withholding tax on interest on External Commercial 
Borrowings (ECBs) has been extended to the IT sector. 
12. IT Enabled Services have been made eligible for Income Tax benefit 
under Sections 10A, 10B and 80HHE of the Income Tax Act.

COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) and (b) The 
operational arm of DoT became a corporation (Bharat Sanchar Nigam 
Limited) on 1.10.2000 and all the assets (including telephone arrears) and 
liabilities of DoT were passed on to BSNL. DoT thus no longer has any 
telephone revenue or revenue arrears on date.

the previous year:  
Year Unpaid bills as on 31st March 
1999-2000 
2000-2001

of the total billed amount each year. 
(c) The reasons for increase in arrears are as follows: 
(i) Unwillingness on the part of subscribers to pay the bills. 
(ii) Bills  issued  correctly   but   perceived  by   the   subscriber   as

(iv) Subscribers not using their dynamic STD lock. 
(d) The various steps taken to recover the telephone revenue arrears are as 
follows: 
1. Telephonic reminders are issued to the defaulting subscribers to clear 
their  dues, failing which their telephones are disconnected. 
2. Telephone Revenue Inspectors and field staff are deputed to visit the 
defaulting subscribers to pursue th e clearing of dues, failing which 
other telephones of the defaulting subscribers are also disconnected. 
3. Incentive is given to staff for ensuring early recovery of outstanding 
dues. 
4. If the above steps do not bring results, recovery suits are filed against 
the defaulters wherever feasible. 
5. Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited sets annual targets for liquidation of 
outstanding for its field units and periodically monitors realisation 
against the targets fixed. Liquidation Boards in each unit/Circle of 
Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited are functioning to liquidate old 
outstanding dues. 
6. As per recent guidelines framed by BSNL, Circles have been 
authorised to utilise the services of the Police, Revenue and other 
Departments of the State Government, whenever necessary, and pay a 
commission of upto 1.5% of the amount recovered.

Competitors in International Long Distance Telephony Sector 
1828. SHRI SURESH PACHOURI: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have considered the recent recommendations of the 
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India not to limit the number of 
competitors in the International Long Distance telephony sector; and 
(b) if so, the details of these recommendations and the action 
taken/proposed to be taken thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The recommendations. of Telecom Regulatory Authority of India 
(TRAI) in respect of opening of Intern ational Long Distance Service (ILDS) 
to private sector have been receive d and accepted by the government. The 
salient features of the recommendations are enclosed as statement. 
Statement 
Salient features of the recommendations of the TRAI for opening of 
International Long Distance Service to private sector. 
* There is no restriction on the number of players. 
* The applicant company shall have networth of Rs. 25 crores. 
65 

RAJYA SABHA [6 December, 2001] 
* The applicant company shall pay one time Entry Fee of Rs. 25 crores. 
* The annual licence fee shall be 15%  of the Adjusted Gross Revenue 
(AGR). 
* The applicant company sh all submit performance Bank 
Guarantee (BG) of Rs. 25 cror es which will be released on 
fulfilment of the roll out obligations. 
* All bearer services are to be provided by the Licensee. 
* The licence is initially valid for a period of 20 years with automatic 
extension by a period of 5 years subject to satisfactory performance in 
accordance with terms & conditions of the licence particularly in regard to 
Quality of Service (QoS) parameters. 
* International long distance traffic should be routed through National 
Long Distance Operators to the Inte rnational Long Distance Operators 
(ILDOs) gateways for onward transmission to International network. 
* The Licensee will establish a minimum of four gateway switches one in 
each region of the country i.e. Eastern, Western, Northern & Southern within 
three years of signing of licence agreement. 
* Delivery of traffic to all the countries in the World is to be ensured 
through at least four Direct Routes i.e. one each to North America, Gulf 
Region, Europe and any one location in Sourth East Asia, Far East and 
Oceania within three years of signing of licence agreement. 
* Two type of Quality of Service (QoS) are permitted.

1843. SHRI K. B. KRISHNA MU RTHY: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Department of Posts conducts National Test Letter Runs 
to test the efficiency of mail sorting and delivery system in metropolitan 
cities; 
(b) if so, whether it was found that almost 50 per cent of the mail was 
delivered late and sorting could not be conducted properly in Chennai, 
Delhi, Hyderabad and Mumbai post offices; and 
(c) whether automatic mail processing systems commissioned in metro 
cities are grossly under-utilised, while extra amount is spent on manual 
sorting? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) The National Test 
Letter Run (NTLR) has been abolished by the Department vide its letter No. 
38-13/99-D dated 15.12.1999 as the NTLR was introduced to assess 
performance of Quick Mail Service which was abolished earlier. The 
Department is however, conducting Live Mail 
90 

[6 December, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
Surveys    to    assess   delivery    efficiency   of   mails    on    a    regular 
basis all over the country. 
(b) No, Sir. As per the results of the Metro Mail Survey 
conducted in September, 2001, th e delivery efficiency of mail 
in Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad and Mumbai is as follows:— 
Chennai 98.9% 
Delhi 98.5% 
Hyderabad 96.1% 
Mumbai 99.1% 
(c) There are two Letter Sorting Machines (LSMs) each in 
the Automatic Mail Processing Centres (AMPCs) at Mumbai 
and Chennai respectively. Out of the two machines, one is 
kept as standby so that the entire volume of mail is not 
delayed in the event of breakdown.

(AMPCs) depends on availability of machinable mails which conform to 
standards of size, length, breadth, thickness, non-use of stapler pin etc.

efforts to popularise the concept of machinable mails and educate the public 
in suitably preparing their mails.

Changes in Foodgrains Procurement Policy 
1863. SHRI A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have effected any change in its procurement 
policy of foodgrains; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any State Governments have supported this programme; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI ASHOK 
PRADHAN):(a) to (d) No, Sir. Under the present policy, Government 
procures all the foodgrains conforming to Fair Average Quality (FAQ) 
specifications through the Food Corporation of India (FCI) and State 
Government Agencies under price sup port operations. However, the farmers 
have the option to sell their produce to FCP/State Government at support 
prices or in the open market, as is advantageous to them. 
However, in order to make the concept of Minimum Support Price a reality 
to all farmers every wher e in the country, the Union Government has been 
persuading States to adopt the scheme  of decentralized procurement. Under 
this scheme, the State Governments would procure, store and distribute food 
grains to meet their requirement for Public Distribution System and other 
welfare schemes. The difference between the economic cost of the State 
118 

[6 December, 2001]        RAJYA SABHA 
Government and Central Issue Price (CIP) is passed on to State Government 
as food subsidy. Government of India would work out a detailed scheme in 
consultation with State Governments to share gains of localized 
procurement. It has been clarified to the States that the scheme would not be 
imposed on any State. The present arrangement would continue where States 
are not yet prepared to shift to a decentralized system of procurement. 
Meetings have been convened with Food Secretaries of Assam, Orissa, 
Bihar, Karnatka, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal, Chattisgarh, 
Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. The Government of 
Assam is willing to implement the scheme. The States were made aware of 
the benefits of decentralized procurement scheme and were asked to submit a 
comprehensive blue print of the proposals required to be addressed, to 
embark on this scheme.

harassments and maltreatment being meted out to the public by the employees 
working in the Food and Supplies Department, particularly in Delhi/New 
Delhi; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI ASHOK 
PRADHAN):(a) and (b) Under the guidelines issued in respect of Antyodaya 
Anna Yojana, State Governments/UT Ad ministrations have been asked to 
identify the poorest of the poor families out of the families living below the 
poverty line (BPL) and issue distinctive ration cards to them by actively 
involving the Panchayati Raj Institutions  (PRIs) in rural areas and local 
bodies in the urban areas. 
(c) and (d) All complaints regardin g malfunctioning of PDS including 
complaints against employees of Food and Supply Department received in

Double role being played by Pakistan 
1907. SHRI C. M. IBRAHIM: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the report 
published in the "Dainik Jagran" New Delhi on November, 3, 2001, to the 
effect that 1,400 Pakistani Jehadis had crossed over to Afghanistan to help 
the Taliban in their fight against the US bombings and its "War against 
terror" and that another 9000 Jehadis had been waiting to cross the border 
along Afghanistan; and 
(b) if so, what steps Government have taken to invite attention of the US 
and other big powers to the double role of side with the US in its fight 
against terrorism while covertly helping the Taliban by looking the otherway 
as Jehadis cross into Afghanistan? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS /SHRI JASWANT 
SINGH): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Government have seen the report appearing in 
the Dainik Jagran on 3rd November, 2001. 
It is widely known that Pakistan decided to show support the campaign in 
Afghanistan against terrorism, because of the extreme international pressure 
that was brought to bear on it, and not out of its own choice. In an address to 
the nation on 19th September, 2001, 
156 

[6 December, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
President Musharraf justified his decision to support the internationl coalition 
against terrorism on the grounds that Pakistan had to protect four critical 
concerns which he identified as Pakistan's security from 'external threats', 
economics revival, protecting Pakistan's nuclear and missile assets, and the 
"Kashmir cause". 
There have been reports of continuing flows of material and men from 
Pakistan, in support of the Taliban regime, despite Pakistan's professed support to 
the action against international terrorism. This gap, between Pakistan's professed 
commitment and the actual situation on the ground, has been widely 
commented upon including in the international media. 
Pakistan authorities are obliged, including under UNSC Resolution, 1373 
on terrorism to refrain from providing any form of support, active or passive, 
and to deny safe havens to entities or persons involved in terrorism.

1926. SHRI KHAGEN DAS:  Will the Minister of LABOUR be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the salient features of the Ce ntrally Sponsored Schemes for 
Rehabilitation of Bonded Labour, Equipment Modernisation and 
Maintenance, Introduction of Trades in  Industrial Training Institute and 
Setting up of new Women's Wing Management Information system, etc.; 
(b) the criteria for allocating funds unde r each scheme to the States and 
corresponding Central share, whether funds are given to the States as 100 per 
cent grant or follow the usual 70/30 (loan/ grant) formula for plan assistance; 
and 
(c) the details of the proposals received, funds released and utilisation for 
the last three years. State-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF LABOUR (SHRI 
MUNI LALL): (a) and (b) The salient features of the Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes are given in Statement-I (See below). 
(c) The State-wise/Scheme-wisc details of the funds released during last 3 
years are given in Statement-II. 
 Statement-I 
Rehabilitation of Bonded Labour: 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourers is 
being operated since May, 1978. Rehabilitation Assistance to the extent of 
Rs. 20,000/- per freed bonded labourer is provided under the Scheme. The 
expenditure is shared by the Central & State Govt, concerned on 50:50 basis. 
Further, under the modified Centrally Sponsored Scheme, which is effective 
from May, 2000. 100% subsidy is give @ Rs. 2 lakh per district for 
conducting surveys of bonded labourers, Rs. 5 lakh per State per annum for 
conducting evaluatory studies and Rs. 10 lakh per State per annum for 
creating 
175 

RAJYA SABHA [6 December, 2001] 
awareness generation relating to abo lition of bonded labour system. The 
expenditure for conducting surveys, evaluatory studies and awareness 
generation programmes are entirely borne by the Central Government and 
there is no State's share in the expenditure on the above components. 
The Central Assistance are released to States on the receipt of complete 
proposals from the States. 
Equipment Modernization and Maintenance, Introduction of Trades in 
Industrial Training Institute and setting up of new women's wings 
Management Information System: 
1. Equipment Modernization Scheme: The objective of the scheme is to 
assist States/UTs in replacing obsolete and outdated equipments and making 
up shortages in the identified 378 ITIs, so that proper equipment is made 
available for training to work on. The expenditure under this scheme is 
shared on 50:50 basis between Central and Statc-Governments. 
2. Establishment of Equipment Maintenance System: Keeping in view the 
large number of Govt. ITI s spread all over the country and the prevailing 
inadequate maintenance system/situation of machinery, it was proposed to 
set up 19 Equipment Maintenance Workshops and 100 Machine 
Maintenance Cells spread all over the country. The expenditure under this 
scheme is shared on 50:50 basis between Central and State Governments. 
3. Introduction of new trade courses in existing ITI s: The main objective 
of the scheme is to expand existing ITI s adequately by introducing new 
based trades, so that these institu tes are in position to produce skilled 
craftsmen, quantitatively and qualitatively to meet specific demands of 
present and future industries. The expenditure under this scheme is shared on 
50:50 basis between the Central and State Governments. 
4. Establishment of new ITI s/Wings for women: The objective of the 
scheme is to expand the Women's Vocational Training Programme, both 
quantitatively and qualitatively to meet the growing skilled manpower 
requirements for Industry, service sector and self employment. 100 ITI 
s/Wings for women have been set up under the scheme. The expenditure 
under this scheme is shared on 50:50 basis between the Central and State 
Governments. 
176 

[6 December, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
5. Establishment of Management Information System: The main objective of 
the scheme is to improve National Vocational Training System planning, 
management and supervision by establishing Management Information 
System, procurement of computer hard ware and software and setting up of 
MIS units at State Directorates. The scheme envisages training of users in the 
application of software developed by NIC. The scheme is 100% funded by 
the Central Government. 
The funds released during last 3 years under different components of the 
project were fully utilized by the States  and no advance funds were released 
to the States during the period.

Draft Approach Paper to the Tenth Plan 
1942. SHRI RUMANDLA RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the PRIME 
MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have approved the draft approach paper to the 
Tenth Five Year Plan; 
(b) if so, whether this plan has already been approved by the National 
Development Council; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken to implement all the projects that were under taken 
during the Ninth Five Year Plan period? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) Yes Sir. 
(b) Yes Sir. 
(c) The Approach Paper to the Tenth Five  Year Plan aims at the stepping 
up the growth rate of GDP to 8% per annum over the Plan period 2002—
2007. It also proposes to establish specific of monitorable targets covering 
economic, social and environmental dimensions of human development. 
These include targets on reduction in  poverty ratio, access to primary 
education, raising literacy rate, decline in infant mortality rate and maternal 
mortality rate, raising employment growth rate, improving coverage of 
villages in terms of access to potable drinking water, reducing gender gaps in 
literacy and wage rates, cleaning of ma jor polluted river stretches, increase 
in forest cover and reducing the decadal population growth rate. 
The Tenth Plan envisages a State wise break up of growth and other 
monitorable targets to build up requisite policy focus for reducing regional 
disparities in social and economic attainments. It proposes to integrate growth 
with equity and social justice. This would involve making agriculture 
development a core element of the Plan. It involves bringing about rapid 
growth in sectors with high quality employment opportunities. It also 
envisages restructuring of targeted programmes, emphasising cross sectoral 
synergies, for special groups. The underlying strategy for the attainment of 
Plan targets is 
193 

RAJYA SABHA [6 December, 2001] 
contingent on our ability to increase investment rate in the economy to 30—
32 per cent, increase the productivity of existing capital assets, undertaking 
second generation policy reforms with a view to improving the efficiency of 
new investment; and devise instrumentalities to facilitate and encourage a 
deepening and broadening of the agenda for reforms across the States. 
Raising the investment rate in the economy is critically tied with the 
ability of the Government both the Central and the States, to undertake an 
agenda for fiscal correction outlined in the Approach Paper. The most crucial 
aspect of this requires the Central Government to increase its savings by 
around 2.9% of GDP. The other important aspect pertains to expediting the 
disinvestment process. 
Improving efficiency of public assets and quality of expenditure in the 
public sector requires rationalisation of Central sector and Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes through convergence, weeding out and transfer of 
schemes to the States. It requires comp letion of existing projects rather than 
intiating new projects, and selectively permitting the use of plan funds for 
critical repair and maintenance activities. Privatisation of non-strategic PSUs 
and closure of non-viable units at both  Centre and States in a time bound 
manner would have to be undertaken. Moreover, expansion of project based 
support to States and making additional central assistance contingent on 
agreed programme of reforms is to be emphasised with a view to improving 
the efficiency of public spending in the States and encourage them to adopt 
agreed agenda for reforms. 
In the context of improving the ef ficiency of public spending, the 
Commission noted the success of the core plan for the States in bringing 
about a more realistic plan formulation both in terms of mobilisation of 
resources and in terms of actual implementation. 
The Approach document r ecognises the serious gaps that are emerging in 
infrastructure particularly in power, railways and public investment in 
irrigation. The flow of private investment in infrastructure has been below 
expectations as in many instances the requisite enabling framework is not yet 
in place. In respect of power 
194 

[6 December, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
sector, the Approach Paper has proposed rationalisation of tariffs through 
SERCs, unbundling generation, transmission and distribution; privatising 
distribution and enabling bulk consumers to access power directly. On 
railways, the Approach Paper has suggested corporatisation of all non core, 
peripheral activities ,of the Indian Railways and establishing an independent 
Rail Tariff Regulatory Authority. 
The Approach Paper has outlined measures to increase efficiency in 
private sector by continuing the reforms in industrial and trade policy, 
undertaking legal and procedural changes to facilitate quick transfer of 
assets, such as repeal of SICA, introduction and strengthening of bankruptcy 
and foreclosure laws etc. It also talks of adopting a blue print for removal of 
administrative, procedural and legal hurdles to investment and improving 
government's interface with the public. Reform and strengthening of judicial 
system and procedure is an area also identified in this context. 
The Approach Paper has identified the need to have a comprehensive land 
use policy to encourage productive utilisation of available land resources. It 
has suggested disbanding export, trade and credit restrictions on agricultural 
and agroforestry products. 
The Panchayati Raj institutions have a critical role to play in the 
developmental framework outlined for the Tenth Plan, particularly with 
regard to improving delivery mechanism for the poverty alleviation 
schemes. They also have special role in improving accountability at the 
local level in the public provisioning of education and health services. 
The Approach Paper places special emphasis on empowerment of   
Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes and on 
mainstreaming of gender concerns. 
195

(d) Completion of ongoing projects has been accorded high priority in the 
Approach Paper to the Tenth Five Year and a moratorium on launching new 
projects until at least a minimum number of partially completed projects are 
brought to completion has been suggested.

1945. SHRI W. ANGOU SINGH: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the steps taken up for formulation of planning from the grass root 
levels; 
(b) the States where the District Planning Committee has been constituted 
and are operational at districts level; and 
(c) the delay in constitution of DPCs and action taken to constitute the 
same within a limited time? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) to (c) Plan formulation from the 
grass root levels has been advocated since the beginning of the planning era. 
The need to break national plan into NationakStatcDistrict'Block and Village 
plans has been recovnised for long. The responsibility for preparation of plans 
for economic development and social justice and its implementation in relation 
to subject listed in the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution 
have been assigned to Panchayats/Urban Local Bodies by the 73rd and 74th 
Constitutional Amendment Acts. This marks a new era in the democratic 
decentralized process by providing constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj 
Institutions. As per Article 243 ZD of the Constitution, the State 
Governments are required to constitute District Planning Committees 
(DPCs) to facilitate the process of decentralized planning. The DPCs are 
expected to consolidate the plans prepared by the Panchayats and the 
Municipalities in the district and to prepare a draft development plan for the 
district as a whole. Not all the States/UTs have constituted DPCs. A 
Conference of Ministers of States in-charge of Panchayati Raj was- held on 
11/07/2001 at New Delhi to discuss measures for strengthening Panchayati 
Raj Institutions. It was resolved in the Conference that DPCs would be set 
up by the remaining Statcs'UTs on priority basis. All the Chief Ministers of 
States and Administrators

National action Plan for development of Backward Districts 
1946. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether Government have formulated any scheme for development of 
backward districts in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any National Action Plan has been chalked out by 
Government in this respect; 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e) Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) to (c) Planning and development 
of an area and allocation of funds for the purpose ar e primarily the 
responsibility of the concerned State Government. Hence, Planning 
Commission has not formulated any scheme for the development of 
backward districts per se nor has any 
203 

RAJYA SABHA [6 December, 2001] 
National Action plan been chalked out. However, the Central Government 
supplements the efforts of the State Governments in the development of 
backward areas through weightage in the formula used for the distribution of 
Central Assistance. 
Further, various programmes have been formulated to deal with the special 
problems of identified areas  such as the Tribal Su b-Plan, the Border Area 
Development Programme, Hill Areas Development Programme, Desert 
Development Programme/Drought Pron e Areas Programme etc. These 
programmes use the special characteris tics of the particular development 
problem to identify the areas and fix the levels of allocation. Further, there 
are a number of programmes for poverty 'alleviation, employment generation, 
infrastructure development, watershed development, social security and land 
reforms to improve the quality of life in the rural areas and to assist people 
below the poverty line. These programmes use poverty/ poverty related 
indicators for the allocation of funds. 
In order to encourage speedy indu strialization and for dispersal of 
industries in industrially backward areas, Category A and Category B 
districts have been identified for the purpose of income tax concessions 
under 80-IA of the Income Tax act. In addition there are various shcmes for 
infrastructure development of the industrial sector such as the Growth 
Centres Scheme, Scheme for Integrated Infrastructural Development 
Centres, etc. 
In addition, successive Finance Co mmissions have laid stress on 
backwardness in the formula for determining inter-state shares of Central 
Tax proceeds. In particular, the weight  of the inverse of per capita state 
income criterion takes note of b ackwardness. The Eleventh Finance 
Commission assigned a weight of 62.5 percent for its award period- 2000-05, 
which is higher than the weight assigned by previous Commissions. In 
addition, the criteria of 'Area' and 'I ndex of Infrastructure' also help 
backward states. In general, larger area and a lower development of 
infrastructure are strongly associated  with backwardness and recognizing 
this, the Eleventh Finance Commission assigned weight of 7.5 per cent each, 
up from 5 per cent recommended by the Tenth Finance Commission. 
Assessing 
204 

[6 December, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
the requirement of revenue-gap grants  is also an exercise which accords 
special consideration to backward stat es. States, which are relatively more 
backward are not able to raise as mu ch of their own revenues as better off 
States. This gets built into the assessment of revenue-gap grants. 
Finance Commissions also take particular note of specific requirements of 
each State during their visits. Su ch requirements are met through 
recommendation of grants for special problems and upgradation and thus 
provide an opportunity to backward states to put forth their claims.

1953. SHRI SOLIPETA RAMACHAN DRA REDDY: Will the Minister 
of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS pleased to state: 
(a) the terms and conditions of the new loans sanctioned by the Asian

KHANDURI): (a) A US $ 240 million loan has been approved by the Asian 
Development Bank (ADB) on 20/9/2001 to the Government of India for

(iii)   Construction   of  4-lane   bypass   at   Brahmsagara,   Harihar, Ranibenneur 
and Haveri.

Disbursement of Credit to SSI by Italy 
1958. SHRI CHO. S. RAMASWAMY:  Will the Minister of SMALL 
SCALE INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Italian Government is disbursing credit to 
promote SSI and medium units in India. 
(b) if so, the amount of funds being given as credit; 
(c) the sectors which are being benefited through this credit; 
(d) the terms and conditions of this credit facility; and 
(e) how many units have applied for this credit and the criteria for 
identifying the units for getting this credit facility? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE 
INDUSTRIES (SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. 
The Italian Government has made available a soft loan of Italian Lira 10 
billion (Rs. 20.00 crores approx.) by  extending a Line of Credit to the 
National Small Industries Corporation Limited. 
(c) This credit is available for acquisition of Italian machinery and services 
related to Leather, Electronics, Plastics, Mechanical, Automobile 
Components, Textile, Food Processing and Packaging, Marble and Granite 
Processing & Extraction sectors. 
(d) The terms and conditions for availing this credit facility are given in 
the Statement (see below). 
(e) Till date seven units have approached NSIC for availing 
assistance. Units with fixed investment of US $ 0.03 to 1.00 million 
are eligible for getting this credit facility. 
212 

[6 December, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
Statement 
Terms & Conditions for availing Italian Credit Line facility 
i.    Eligibility: 
Any enterprise with fixed investment in the order of US $ 0.03 
to 1.0 million. The enterprise should be equipped or is willing to 
equip its plant in the short term with a quality system conforming 
to international standard ISO-9000. For this purpose only the 
original value of the fixed assets installed or proposed to be 
installed shall be taken into account. Value of single assistance in 
the selected sectors (referred to a single beneficiary) shall be 
higher than 50 million Italian Liras (equivalent Rs. 10.00 lakhs 
approx.). In case of assistance fo r projects other than the selected 
sectors the value of every single contract shall be higher than 300 
million Italian Liras (Rs. 60.00 lakhs approx.) 
In    order    to    enlarge    the number    of    potential 
beneficiaries an upper limit of Italian Lira 2.5  billion 
(equivalent   to   Rs.   5.00   crores approx.)   for   a   single 
contract has been set. 
ii.    Application Fee: 
The application fee (non refundable) is Rs. 1000/-payable by 
Account Payee Bank Draft in favour of 'NSIC LIMITED' 
iii.    Repayment: 
The period of repayment is 7 years in 28 quarterly installments 
with gestation period of 18 months. 
iv.    Rate of Interest: 
The rate of interest is 9% p.a. 
213 

RAJYA SABHA [6 December, 2001] 
v.      Earnest money & service charges: 
The earnest money is 15% of the cost of machine and service  
charges are 2% of the cost of machine.  
vi.    Payment to supplier: 
Under the terms of Credit Line, a letter of credit is not required 
to be opened in favour of the Italian Suppliers. On approval of 
the project proposal by the Italian Authorities the supplier shall 
be intimated that funds have been earmarked which would be 
released on supply of machine as  per the terms agreed between 
the Indian buyer and the Italian supplier. 
vii COLLATERAL SECURITY: 
1. For units seeking assistance under Italian credit Line and 
Tannery modernisation scheme of Govt, of India. 
* In addition to the earnest money of 15% the unit shall pay a 
further fixed deposit of 15% of the cost of machinery with 
NSIC before delivery of the machine. 
* The Government's contribution by way of capital subsidy 
under tannery modernisation scheme shall also be made 
available to NSIC. 
* The machine purchased under the credit line shall be 
mortgaged with NSIC. 
2. For units seeking assistance under Italian Credit & not 
covered under Tannery modernisation scheme of Govt, of 
India. 
* In addition to the earnest money of 15% the unit shall pay a 
further fixed deposit of 25% of the cost of machine with 
NSIC before delivery of the machine. 
* For units not able to mobilise the additional 25% for further 
fixed deposit, shall be required to provide immovable 
property as security at least equal to 50% of the value of 
assistance after adjusting earnest money for machinery 
purchased. 
* The machine purchased under the credit line shall be 
mortgaged with NSIC.
